00:00:00 - Maya Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick roll call. Uh, we got Daniel and Ravi from our side. Could folks from NovaPay say hi?
00:00:10 - Laura Chen: Hi, Laura here. Owen and Priya with me. Good to see you all.
00:00:18 - Maya Patel: Great. Agenda — throughput results, tuning suggestions, and next steps. We have 45 minutes.
00:00:30 - Daniel Kim: Quick recap — last week we ran the 1-hour burst tests with the default batching and saw p95 around 480ms at 200 concurrency, throughput ~3.2k tok/s, but under sustained load latency crept up. We suspect batching and queueing config.
00:01:00 - Owen Martinez: Right, in our env we saw tail latencies spike after about 15 minutes, memory pressure on the worker pods increased, some request retries. We sent the logs to you.
00:01:18 - Ravi Shah: Yep we saw retries; looks like KV cache warmup was low — our profiler shows cache hit rate ~22% initially. Could be due to ephemeral pods or small prefix reuse.
00:01:40 - Priya Rao: Quick note — we run varied seq lengths, avg 80 tokens but heavy tail to 1024 for some customers. So batch sizing needs to account for that.
00:02:00 - Daniel Kim: That distribution matters a lot. Continuous batching is usually beneficial if sequence length distribution is tight; with heavy tail we recommend dynamic shaping — group short sequences for large batches, route long ones to lower latency lanes.
00:02:22 - Laura Chen: Question — for the POC, are we testing hosted or Dedicated? We want to see Dedicated numbers for cost reasons.
00:02:35 - Maya Patel: For the POC we're doing Redwood hosted with a Dedicated-equivalent config (we emulate 4x A100 load). But we can spin dedicated nodes on your VPC for a later run.
00:02:50 - Owen Martinez: Ok. On the config we care about concurrency target — what's a reasonable concurrent request number per GPU?
00:03:02 - Daniel Kim: Depends on model and quant. For the open 7B we saw best econ at 256–512 concurrent when using continuous batching + KV cache. For 13B it drops to 128–256. Those are starting points.
00:03:20 - Samir Desai: Are these numbers per GPU or per node? We have multi-GPU nodes.
00:03:26 - Daniel Kim: Per accelerator. If you have 8x chips per node, you scale horizontally. But also pay attention to per-node memory and network.
00:03:38 - Priya Rao: We noticed queue depth grows — at 200 concurrency queueing backlog reached roughly 800 requests, which then caused retries. Is there a recommended queueing strategy?
00:03:50 - Ravi Shah: We recommend a two-tier queue: fast path for warm cache and short seqs with a tight concurrency cap; a slow path with more buffering for long seqs and batch accumulation. Also an admission controller to shed load gracefully or fallback to cheaper model variants.
00:04:10 - Laura Chen: That makes sense. Can you explain how the KV cache warmup is measured? Our logs show inconsistent numbers.
00:04:22 - Daniel Kim: Sure — we measure prefix frequency and repeated context reuse. The profiler reports KV cache hits per token; as clients repeat prompts or have conversational turns the cache hit goes up. If pods are short-lived you lose cache warmup. We saw low hit rates during your early tests.
00:04:40 - Owen Martinez: Our pods are scaled down aggressively. Could that be hurting us?
00:04:45 - Maya Patel: Yes, aggressive autoscale can increase cold starts. For throughput we recommend longer-lived workers or keeping a small warm pool. Also consider sticky routing for conversational sessions.
00:05:00 - Daniel Kim: For the benchmark we're proposing a 6-hour continuous run at 512 concurrency for your typical mix; that will reveal steady-state behavior and cache warmup.
00:05:12 - Samir Desai: Is 512 realistic? That sounds high for production.
00:05:16 - Daniel Kim: It's a stress test to measure where queueing and kernel saturation happen. We'll also run a 256 run as a mid point.
00:05:24 - Priya Rao: What metrics will you collect? We need things we can map to our dashboards.
00:05:30 - Daniel Kim: We'll collect p50/p90/p95/p99 latencies, throughput tok/s, GPU util, per-kernel timings, KV cache hit/miss, queue depth, and retry rates. We'll export profiler flamegraphs and a CSV.
00:05:44 - Laura Chen: Perfect. Also can you share the kernel breakdown? Our infra team cares about memory and comms.
00:05:50 - Ravi Shah: Yes we'll include per-kernel time slices. One caveat — profiler names sometimes get munged in auto-transcripts; you might see e.g., K-V cash or memcopy spelled weirdly in the export.
00:06:02 - Owen Martinez: Haha noted. Any quick tuning steps we can try on our side before the long run?
00:06:08 - Daniel Kim: A few. 1) Increase worker idle timeout so the warm pool stays alive; 2) enable session-level sticky routing for convs; 3) set a soft concurrency cap per worker to avoid huge queues; 4) enable prefix cache pre-warm for common prompts. We'll send exact config snippets.
00:06:26 - Maya Patel: I'll email the snippets and the Dedicated sizing recommendation after this call.
00:06:30 - Laura Chen: On cost — if we go Dedicated with 4x A100 equivalent, what's ballpark monthly?
00:06:36 - Maya Patel: I'll send a pricing sheet but rough ballpark in our last estimate: $XXk–$YYk depending on commit. I'll get you a formal quote by tomorrow.
00:06:48 - Owen Martinez: Competitors — we did a quick run on Vertex and saw lower latency at low concurrency but cost scaled badly. Any thoughts?
00:06:56 - Daniel Kim: That's common; Vertex uses different batching strategies and autoscaling. Our angle is perf per dollar at steady-state with batching + cache. We'll include a comparison note.
00:07:10 - Priya Rao: Back to queueing, do you support dynamic priority? E.g., payment flows get priority over low-value queries.
00:07:18 - Ravi Shah: Yes, route policies can be set per route with priority weights; lower priority can be batched more aggressively or sent to cost-tiered models. We'll demo policy config in a follow-up.
00:07:30 - Laura Chen: Great. Any security blockers we should worry about for the Dedicated test?
00:07:36 - Maya Patel: For Dedicated in VPC we support SSO, SAML, customer KMS, and audit logs. Priya, you flagged compliance items earlier?
00:07:44 - Priya Rao: Mainly audit retention and KMS integration. We'll need to confirm retention windows.
00:07:50 - Maya Patel: Noted — I'll add that to the list.
00:08:00 - Daniel Kim: Ok switching to the numbers we collected: earlier 1-hour test CSV is in the drive link we sent. Highlights: p95 at 480ms at 200 concurrency, p99 ~1.6s; throughput increased with batch size up to a point then plateaued; memory spikes corresponded to large batch assembly.
00:08:22 - Owen Martinez: Can you share the batch size distribution? We want to see effective batch sizes over time.
00:08:28 - Daniel Kim: Yes — in that run effective batch size averaged 12 for short seqs and 3 for long seqs; under stress it dropped as queueing misbehaved.
00:08:40 - Samir Desai: Is there a knob to limit max batch assembly latency so requests don't wait too long for a full batch?
00:08:46 - Ravi Shah: Yes set a max assemble wait (we call it batch_wait_ms) — tradeoff latency vs throughput. We typically start at 12ms for low-latency apps, 30–50ms for batchy throughput.
00:09:00 - Laura Chen: Can we try lowering batch_wait_ms to 15ms and raise concurrency cap to 300 to see if tail improves?
00:09:08 - Daniel Kim: We can. We'll run a short test matrix: (batch_wait_ms 12/15/30) x (concurrency 200/300/512) to sample the surface.
00:09:18 - Maya Patel: We'll log the experiment config in the shared spreadsheet.
00:09:22 - Owen Martinez: About cache warmup — you recommended sticky routing. Any downside?
00:09:28 - Daniel Kim: Slightly reduced balancing efficiency on very bursty traffic, but significant cache benefit for convs. You can do hybrid: sticky per-session for high-value routes, round-robin for others.
00:09:42 - Priya Rao: For fallback models — if primary saturated, can you automatically route to cheaper quantized variant?
00:09:48 - Ravi Shah: Yes, we support model variant routing by policy. The output quality degrades a bit but keeps SLAs. We'll show quality vs cost tradeoffs.
00:10:00 - Laura Chen: Ok. On next steps you mentioned a 6-hour run. When can this happen?
00:10:06 - Daniel Kim: We can start Friday morning PST, but need your traffic sample to seed the runner. If you can provide the trace by Thursday, we can run Friday and have results Monday.
00:10:18 - Owen Martinez: We'll try to get the trace by Thursday.
00:10:22 - Maya Patel: I'll make the job and post the run config.
00:10:26 - Samir Desai: Any expectations on p95 for the steady run?
00:10:30 - Daniel Kim: Hard to promise — if cache warms to 60–70% hit and batches average 10 for short seqs, p95 should be under 400–450ms at 512 for 7B. But 13B will be higher.
00:10:44 - Laura Chen: Noted.
00:10:50 - Priya Rao: A couple of clarifying Qs from SRE: do we need to open any ports for profiler or will you ship artifacts?
00:10:58 - Daniel Kim: We'll run the profiler from within the cluster; we might ask for temporary SSH jumpbox or agent access. If you prefer, we can provide self-collect scripts and you can upload artifacts.
00:11:10 - Owen Martinez: We'll prefer self-collect scripts. Security team dislikes external agents.
00:11:16 - Maya Patel: We'll prepare scripts and docs.
00:11:20 - Daniel Kim: Ok jumping ahead — on the fallback model idea, we have a recommended quantization profile that keeps latency low with small quality delta; we can A/B test that in the benchmark.
00:11:32 - Laura Chen: Sounds good. Can you also include a cost model showing cost per 1M requests?
00:11:38 - Maya Patel: Yes, we'll update the cost model with the benchmark and Dedicated sizing.
00:11:44 - Priya Rao: Any gotchas from network egress? We have cross-region traffic occasionally.
00:11:50 - Ravi Shah: For latency-sensitive, keep inference in-region; cross-region adds unpredictable tail. We'll surface region routing policies.
00:12:00 - Owen Martinez: Good point. Ok I think we're aligned on the runs and data needed.
00:12:06 - Laura Chen: Quick recap before we close?
00:12:10 - Maya Patel: Recap: Redwood to run 6-hour continuous benchmark at 512 concurrency and a short matrix, share profilers and kernel timings; NovaPay to send 24h traffic trace and seq len histogram; Maya to send Dedicated sizing and pricing; Priya to confirm KMS/audit retention.
00:12:28 - Owen Martinez: Yep. We'll aim to send trace Thursday.
00:12:32 - Maya Patel: Great — next sync, we'll review the benchmark results. Any final questions?
00:12:38 - Samir Desai: None from me.
00:12:40 - Laura Chen: All good. Thanks everyone.
00:12:44 - Maya Patel: Thanks. Ending recording.
